sections.start: Measured four ways — maximum and minimum height of the front pocket, and of the back pocket — the two halves of the garment tell different stories.
sections.serves: A set of front- and back-pocket measurements taken from jeans sold by 21 popular brands finds a layout that is nearly identical at the back of the garment and strikingly different at the front: men's front pockets run about nine inches deeper than women's.
sections.how: It reports average maximum front-pocket heights of 23.13 in for men versus 14.33 in for women, while back height and width differ by less than an inch and front width differs much less.

sections.start: The averages could hide a wide overlap.
sections.serves: A set of front- and back-pocket measurements taken from jeans sold by 21 popular brands finds a layout that is nearly identical at the back of the garment and strikingly different at the front: men's front pockets run about nine inches deeper than women's.
sections.how: It plots every pair and reports ranges and medians showing almost no overlap, then notes that women's front pockets are often shorter than their back pockets while men's never are.

sections.start: The obvious suspects are the garment's shape and its price.
sections.serves: A set of front- and back-pocket measurements taken from jeans sold by 21 popular brands finds a layout that is nearly identical at the back of the garment and strikingly different at the front: men's front pockets run about nine inches deeper than women's.
sections.how: It shows women's skinny, straight and boot-cut averages are nearly identical, and price correlates −0.08 with front-pocket height, so neither style nor price explains the gap.

sections.start: Within women's jeans, the brand averages fan out from 12.00 in at Guess and 12.35 in at Levi's to 19.75 in at Abercrombie.
sections.how: It compares women's brand averages and shows even the highest brand, Abercrombie at 19.75 in, stays below the men's average of 23.13 in, with most brands clustering between 13 and 15 in.
